doc.title: Javon Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Which concerts were cancelled and calling the sidemen
summary: Thailand trips, then cancelled festivals and college dates; phone calls to bandmates are commiserating.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well let me see, ‘cause interestingly enough I went to Thailand twice in January. I went in the early part of January and I went at the end of January into early February. And then I played — no that’s not true. I went to Thailand in late January and late February into March. And so I got back March 2 and I haven’t played a concert since. So I was due to play the Saratoga Jazz Festival this year, that’s been cancelled of course, the festival; the San Jose Jazz Festival, that’s been postponed to next year; various venues that I was going to be playing at, there was a concert/festival I’ve been doing in Arizona, Prescott, Arizona got cancelled. So it’s just been a slew of performances, concerts, college performances at Michigan State University. There was just so many different things. But most all of them actually have been either postponed or — well not, postponed and the date has gone along with that postponement. And so all we can do from there is see how it turns out for the next year.
I’m assuming that for some of these things you had engaged sidemen, sidepeople, and that then you have to make that phone call to them. How did that feel?

Well again, we’re all experiencing it and I’m not the only one that’s getting the phone call or giving the phone call. They’re getting phone calls from multiple people so there’s a certain amount of understanding. Again this is in territory that none of us have ever been in before. So we just sit and we kind of commiserate about the situation, we find a way to have some laughter before we get off the phone and we just kind of press on and hope for the best and just wait for that opportunity to perform.
